chunks: Abu Basir asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a man in ihram who looked at a woman's leg or her private part and ejaculated, so he said:
"If he is wealthy, then a camel is incumbent upon him; if he is of moderate means, then a cow is incumbent upon him; and if he is poor, then a sheep is incumbent upon him."
And he said: "I did not impose this upon him because he ejaculated, but rather I imposed it upon him because he looked at what was not halal for him."

key_terms.سَاقِ: the leg, mentioned here as the object of unlawful gaze
key_terms.لَا يَحِلُّ لَهُ: what is not lawful for him to look at
key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: a person in the state of ihram during hajj or 'umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the kaffarah for a person in ihram who looks unlawfully at a woman and ejaculates?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a muhrim who looks at a woman unlawfully and ejaculates, assigning an expiation according to his financial capacity. The Imam عليه السلام clarifies that the liability is due to the forbidden gaze itself, not merely the emission.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2590 - Abu Basir asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a Muhrim (one in a state of Ihram) who looked at the leg of a woman or her private part and ejaculated.
Imam (as) said: "If he is wealthy, he must offer a camel. If he is of moderate means, he must offer a cow. If he is poor, he must offer a sheep."
Imam (as) added: "I have not imposed this upon him because he ejaculated, but because he looked at what was unlawful for him."
